- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, increase forecast slope to match sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model often fails to adjust — apply downward bias correction in next 5–7 days.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, model is underestimating — increase forecast by 2–5% per day until trend stabilizes.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and true outcome shows volatility, model often underreacts — add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast to capture hidden momentum.
